acceptanceCriteria: A first configured release start applies the persisted default true preference before routine reporting; Android/iOS automatic collection remains manifest/plist disabled until this explicit application.
A stored opt-out or opt-in is restored on process restart, and changing the Settings switch persists and applies the new preference immediately through a typed, non-racy command.
Debug, preview and automated test environments force collection off regardless of the stored user preference; absence or failure of optional Firebase configuration never blocks startup.
The coordinator exposes deterministic Active, Off by choice, Disabled in this build and Unavailable states for later Settings integration.
The production bridge exposes only collection enablement and reviewed technical non-fatals; no Analytics, user IDs, breadcrumbs, user content or external project/secret is introduced.

Platform tests cover release default-on, restart restore, live disable/re-enable, non-release disabling, unavailable/failed drivers and the minimal iOS bridge contract. Specialist does not run Gradle.
goal: Harden the platform-neutral crash runtime contract for synchronous startup/live preference application, deterministic effective state, forced non-release disabling and an exportable minimal iOS native driver bridge without requiring Firebase configuration.
